sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's tech sector is decoupling from US peers, with local names like YELO and ELIT driving outsized gains on domestic retail flows and limited foreign participation.
Structural adoption of digital payments and e-commerce in tier-2/3 cities continues to underpin revenue growth for ID-listed tech firms, making them less sensitive to global rate cycles.
Regulatory tailwinds from the OJK's fintech sandbox and government digitalization push create a durable pipeline for small-cap tech listings and M&A activity.
sectors.ai: Buy YELO and ELIT on momentum but take profits into strength; rotate into ASGR for value exposure as ID tech outperforms US. Monitor CRWD for US sentiment spillover, but keep ID names as core. Trim PMUI after the pop—liquidity risk is high. Position sizing matters; the signal is normal, so avoid leverage.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rupiah depreciation structurally favors domestic producers with local raw-material sourcing, boosting competitiveness against imported FMCG goods.
Rising Indonesian food inflation and middle-class consumption growth sustain demand for affordable staples, benefiting low-priced mass-market brands.
Consolidation in fragmented sub-sectors (snacks, oils, agar) creates M&A upside for small caps with strong distribution networks.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian FMCG names with direct commodity or import-substitution exposure (SRSN, OILS, AGAR) as rupiah weakness and food-price inflation drive margin tailwinds; avoid US-linked consumer plays. Rotate into small-cap staples with volume growth and pricing power ahead of Q3 earnings, targeting 15-20% upside over 8-12 weeks.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's infrastructure names are decoupling from US peers, driven by domestic capex cycle and government project disbursements, making local exposure a structural alpha source.
Small-cap movers (ASLI, LEAD) show speculative liquidity churn, but SSIA and SULI offer earnings-backed growth tied to property and steel demand from new capital projects.
The NORMAL signal suggests mean-reversion risk; favor names with confirmed order books over pure momentum plays to avoid sharp reversals.
sectors.ai: Buy ASLI and LEAD on momentum, but treat as trade-only given 20-25% spikes without earnings confirmation. Rotate into SSIA and SULI for relative value as aggregate signal stays NORMAL. Trim US-exposed names like PACK on the -0.88% divergence. Watch BALI for follow-through; if it holds +11%, add. Overall, stay selective—infrastructure is flat, so pick idiosyncratic winners, not beta.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's e-commerce and last-mile delivery expansion continues to structurally lift small-cap logistics names like PPGL and SOCI, independent of global trade weakness.
Commodity export logistics (coal, nickel, palm oil) remains a durable driver for heavy-equipment and trucking firms (TRUK, HUMI), supported by sustained mining output and infrastructure spend.
Government port and toll-road capex, plus the new capital city (IKN) build-out, creates multi-year demand for integrated logistics providers, favoring NELY and TAXI as direct beneficiaries.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in PPGL, SOCI, and NELY as domestic logistics outperformance (+1.02% ID vs -0.04% US) signals resilient e-commerce and commodity-driven demand; rotate into TRUK and WINS for mid-cap upside. Maintain WATCH but add on any 3-5% dips, targeting 10-15% gains over 3 months as volume confirms.

Franchise and food-service models, including PZZA and NATO, benefit from urbanization and premiumization trends, though margin pressure from input costs remains a watch item.

Favor momentum in DOOH and SINI for near-term upside, but trim PZZA and IBOS on valuation risk. Maintain WATCH for pullback entries, targeting 2-4 week horizon.
